title: Provenance integrity
promise: Current, not stale: when a decision changes, the old value is kept as traceable history, never lost and never served as current.
question: When a decision has changed, does memory_trace give back its complete, correctly ordered history, each version tied to the message that said it?
method: 44 hand-written decision histories (34 changed 1-2 times, 10 never changed) stored through the public API, one structured decision_made claim per message; then the real memory_trace tool (handle_memory_trace, session 'default') per history. Scored against documented behaviour, not current output. Deterministic, lexical mode, no LLM.

headline.label: changed decisions with a fully correct trace

metrics.name: complete
metrics.definition: the trace holds exactly the history's values, one version each

metrics.name: ordered
metrics.definition: versions in decision order; exactly one live version, the current one

metrics.name: grounded
metrics.definition: each version's source message contains that version's value

metrics.name: edges
metrics.definition: each older version superseded by the next with the documented edge type

metrics.name: unchanged-correct
metrics.definition: a never-changed decision traces to one live version, no supersession

tables.title: Stress: subject drift (final change saved under a reworded subject)
columns: old subject traces to current value
old subject's trace flags the new value

tables.title: Edge types on the per-change traces

versions.source_text: Decision: we will use PostgreSQL 15 for the orders-service database.
Update: going forward, the orders-service database is SQLite.

limits: Hand-written synthetic histories, one author; every value is stored as a structured claim, so extraction quality is not tested here.
All changes come from the user; assistant-sourced changes and the trust guard are covered by the supersession matrix, not this eval.
Subject drift is an expected limitation: decisions are linked by subject name, not by meaning.
findings: subject drift: trace of the original subject still names the outdated value as current in 34/34 histories; the new subject's trace has no history in 34/34; the old subject's trace lists the newer value under conflicts in 0/34 (LIPI Logic: decisions are linked by subject words, memcontext/conflicts.py:51 live_same_kind; reworded subjects share none)
coverage gap: no history changes to a token-subset of its old value, so the REFINES edge (memcontext/supersession.py:52) is never exercised here
